gen-mystery-quest-gf-roboto: Nostalgic and bookish, Mystery Quest keeps its curves open and its ascenders compact. Roboto, a sans-serif with generous round mouths, steps back; make the heading small and its character fades, or the body large and it takes over.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-ruda: Bookish nostalgia lives in the compact ascenders and gaping curves of Mystery Quest. Ruda's monoline strokes, like bent wire, and sizable x-height let text run on easily across a screen.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-saira: Open curves and compact ascenders give Mystery Quest a bookish, nostalgic voice that grabs attention. And Saira, a sans-serif with see-through s shapes, does the quieter work of carrying text cleanly.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-sarpanch: Bookish and nostalgic, with open curves and compact ascenders. Sarpanch, a sans-serif with a clearly open e, gives that display heading a contemporary, approachable partner underneath, one that stays out of its way.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk brings big, open-looking e and a shapes and terminals that never close in, beneath the bookish, nostalgic Mystery Quest. Friendly openness is what ties them together.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-sen: Mystery Quest wears its bookish, nostalgic mood through gaping curves and compact ascenders, built to be looked at. Sen, with letterforms like bent tubing and a constant-weight line, is the one built to be read.
